candidate_name: Jamaica Energy Partners onshore LNG storage terminal
sponsor_or_proposer: Jamaica Energy Partners (JEP) Group / InterEnergy Group
current_state: Planning / due-diligence phase as of Jan 2026. JEP (InterEnergy subsidiary, ~1/3 of Jamaica's power) announced a >US$150M plan triggered by Hurricane Melissa: a US$80-110M onshore LNG storage terminal plus ~US$50M to convert two thermal plants (124 MW Dr Bird, St Catherine; 66 MW West Kingston Power Partners, Kingston) from HFO to gas. Stated purpose is to give customers a backup gas source when the single Excelerate Old Harbour FSRU must evacuate during hurricanes. CEO McKenzie: 'We're still doing the due diligence on the numbers.' 24-month timeline to commercial ops (~early 2028). An undisclosed strategic partner is identified.
missing_threshold_elements: Concrete step: no MOU/FEED/permit/site lease/FID disclosed - explicitly 'still doing due diligence,' planning phase only. Location: onshore Jamaica, Kingston/St Catherine area implied (tied to Dr Bird + West Kingston plants) but the specific storage-terminal site is not stated. Scope ambiguity: described as an onshore LNG *storage* terminal backing up the FSRU rather than a classic import/regas terminal - may sit at the small-scale/distribution edge of GEM terminal scope; confirm against the methodology terminal definition before any add.
watch_for: MOU/EPC contract signed; site selection/land lease; environmental permit application; disclosure of the strategic partner; FID; capacity figure in MTPA. Re-check ~Q1 2027.
